source: W. Wang et al., 'Blast resistance of reinforced concrete slabs based on residual load-bearing capacity', Materials 15(18), 6449 (2022), doi:10.3390/ma15186449, PMC9502281
licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Derived data: values transcribed from the paper's text, Tables 1-5 and Figure 1; nothing digitised from plots.

slabs.orientation: upright, centre 0.7 m above the ground, clamped at the corners with plates welded between, 'fixed on four sides'
slabs.bars: HRB400, both ways in both faces at 100 mm (Figure 1), 4 mm HPB235 ties
slabs.cover: the text's 50 mm is a misprint; Figure 1 marks 13 mm, and the ratios put the bars 80 mm from the far face
slabs.concrete: C30, by grade only (the paper's own model used 30 MPa and 2,300 kg/m3)

charge.kind: bare sphere of TNT and RDX (4:6 by mass) with aluminium, centrally initiated
charge.note: the TNT equivalence is the paper's; what it was matched to is not stated

pressure_gauges.on: a separate steel plate placed as the slabs were

displacements.on: the slabs' back faces, pen-type gauges, top to bottom (Figures 5 and 6 sketch their places)

damage.A: front intact; back cracked both ways, oblique shear cracks at both ends, concrete broken near an edge, bars exposed
damage.B: front intact; fine cracks both ways at the back
